questions.topicName: Structure, Function, and Disorders of the Thymus
questions.stem: In the right-hand radiograph, the arrow marks a mediastinal contour abnormality causing loss of the upper-left heart border silhouette. In which compartment is this thymic mass located?

explanation.summary: A thymic mass lies in the anterior mediastinum; a lateral view would confirm the anterior/retrosternal location, and loss of the upper heart-border silhouette localizes it anteriorly.
explanation.whyCorrect: A thymic mass lies in the anterior mediastinum; a lateral view would confirm the anterior/retrosternal location, and loss of the upper heart-border silhouette localizes it anteriorly.

questions.topicName: Structure, Function, and Disorders of the Thymus
questions.stem: These histologic fields are from a slow-growing anterior mediastinal tumor in an adult. Patients with this tumor are at increased risk of which associated condition?

explanation.summary: The images show thymoma; about half of thymoma patients have myasthenia gravis, an autoimmune disease with antibodies against the neuromuscular junction.
explanation.whyCorrect: The images show thymoma; about half of thymoma patients have myasthenia gravis, an autoimmune disease with antibodies against the neuromuscular junction.

questions.topicName: Structure, Function, and Disorders of the Thymus
questions.stem: This diffuse skin finding on the trunk of a young boy, together with recurrent infections and easy bruising from small platelets, is part of the triad of which X-linked disorder?

explanation.summary: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome is an X-linked recessive WAS-gene disorder with the triad of eczema, recurrent infections (hypoplastic thymus), and thrombocytopenia with small platelets.
explanation.whyCorrect: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome is an X-linked recessive WAS-gene disorder with the triad of eczema, recurrent infections (hypoplastic thymus), and thrombocytopenia with small platelets.

questions.topicName: Structure, Function, and Disorders of the Thymus
questions.stem: This diagram depicts the fate of developing T cells based on how strongly their receptors bind self-antigen. What is the primary purpose of eliminating cells that bind self-antigen with high affinity?

choices.label: B
choices.text: To establish central tolerance and prevent autoimmunity

choices.label: C
choices.text: To promote clonal proliferation of effector cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: To generate red blood cell precursors

explanation.summary: T cells that bind self-antigen too strongly are deleted (negative selection) so that autoreactive cells do not enter the circulation; this central tolerance prevents autoimmune disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: T cells that bind self-antigen too strongly are deleted (negative selection) so that autoreactive cells do not enter the circulation; this central tolerance prevents autoimmune disease.
